channel.title: The Center For Michigan | Bridge Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Center For Michigan | Bridge Magazine (thecenterformichigan.net)

item.title: Michigan athletes go for gold in Winter Olympics. Who and when to watch
item.description: More than a dozen athletes with Michigan ties qualified for the 2026 Winter Olympics in Italy. The state is particularly well represented in ice dancing and hockey.

item.title: Opinion | The youth literacy crisis is a threat to the nation’s foundation
item.description: Literacy achievements come about through a fierce commitment to evidence-based practices and hard work by teachers, students, and families. They are proof that all students can read when they are afforded the proper resources.

item.title: Gretchen Whitmer seeks $625M for literacy, tax ‘holiday’ for school supplies
item.description: Gov. Gretchen Whitmer is expected to pitch more funding for literacy and a pair of targeted tax breaks during her final budget proposal Wednesday.

item.title: Ice grips Great Lakes, with Erie nearly fully covered
item.description: About 95% percent of Lake Erie is covered in ice, and even half of Lake Superior is too. Bitter cold temperatures have spurred major ice coverage across the Great Lakes, but warmer weather is coming.

item.title: Michigan cash-for-moms program launches in Detroit, expanding in UP
item.description: Applications are open in Detroit. In March, the popular cash aid program is slated to grow across the rest of Michigan's Upper Peninsula.

item.title: In bid for governor, John James proposes ‘bill of rights’ for Michigan parents
item.description: In a new 'bill of rights' for Michigan parents, GOP gubernatorial candidate John James proposes opting into a private school choice program and limiting transgender athletes.

item.title: Michigan public university tuition tops $17K on avg.; financial aid can save 47%
item.description: Tuition at public universities has gone up in tandem with state funding cuts years ago but federal and state grants, along with funding from universities to students, cut costs to a student on average by nearly half.

item.title: Michigan’s harsh winter and school closings: What to know
item.description: When the forecast turns extremely cold or snowy, superintendents call school off. It prompts cheers from students and some headaches for the school calendar.

item.title: Trump threatens to block Michigan-Canada bridge in trade war escalation
item.description: President Donald Trump suggests he ‘will not allow’ the nearly completed Gordie Howe International Bridge to open in Detroit because of an ongoing trade war with Canada.

item.title: Jury convicts in signature fraud scandal that rocked 2022 Michigan governor race
item.description: Jury finds two men guilty of conducting a criminal enterprise for fraudulent petition signatures that kept five governor candidates of Michigan's 2022 ballot.
